name: James (Jesus' brother)
title: Leader of Jerusalem and Pillar of Righteousness
summary: James was Jesus' brother and became one of the most prominent leaders in the early church in Jerusalem. He was known for his piety and righteousness, and wrote the Epistle of James in the New Testament. He played a crucial role at the Council of Jerusalem and was martyred around the year 62.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among Jesus' brothers
keyEvents.description: James is mentioned as one of Jesus' brothers along with Joses, Simon and Judas. They did not believe in Jesus during his public ministry.

keyEvents.title: The risen Jesus appears to James
keyEvents.description: Paul writes that Jesus appeared to James after the resurrection, which likely led to his conversion and faith.

keyEvents.title: Recognized as a pillar in the church
keyEvents.description: Paul describes James, together with Peter and John, as pillars in the church in Jerusalem. They gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship.

keyEvents.title: Leads the apostolic council in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: James played a decisive role at the apostolic council where the question of Gentiles' relationship to the Mosaic Law was settled. He formulated the final decision.

keyEvents.title: Meets Paul in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: When Paul came to Jerusalem after his missionary journeys, he met James and the elders to report on his work among the Gentiles.

keyEvents.title: Author of the Letter of James
keyEvents.description: James wrote a letter to the twelve tribes in the diaspora, with practical teaching about faith and works, the power of the tongue and wisdom from God.
